question.problem: The parabola $y={x}^{2}+x$ and the line $y=3x-1$ intersect at a single point with coordinates $(p,q).$ What is $p+q?$
question.worked_solution:
We need to solve the following system consisting of the equations of the curves:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}y={x}^{2}+x \\ y=3x-1\end{aligned}
$$

Setting the equations equal to one another and solving, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+x & =3x-1 \\ {x}^{2}+x-3x+1 & =0 \\ {x}^{2}-2x+1 & =0 \\ (x-1)(x-1) & =0 \\ x & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the $x$-coordinate of the intersection point is $x=1.$ 

To find the $y$-coordinate of the intersection point, we plug this value into either curve. 
Let's choose the equation of the line. Substituting $x=1,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =3x-1 \\  & =3(1)-1 \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the only point of intersection is $(1,2).$ Therefore, $p=1,\,q=2,$ and 

$$
p+q=1+2=3.
$$
